LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level scope of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `prepare()` or `package()`. In this file, the global variable assignments are limited to standard metadata (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, `sha256sums`) and two derived variables: `_image` and `_pkgbasename`.

The variable `_image` is defined using command substitution: `_image="$(basename "${source[0]}")"`. While command substitution in the global scope can be dangerous if it executes untrusted code, in this case it only runs `basename` on the first entry of the `source` array, which is a static HTTPS URL pointing to a release asset on GitHub. There is no network access, code execution, or data exfiltration during this operation. The input is a literal string known at parse time, and `basename` is a safe, local utility.

All other aspects of the PKGBUILD's global scope are static assignments. No suspicious downloads, evals, or external network calls occur during sourcing. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>

<summary>No dangerous top-level code execution</summary>
